note_text: China accounts for approximately 25% of global output in advanced industries and 24% of high-technology manufacturing. https://itif.org/publications/2026/05/06/china-produces-nearly-one-quarter-global-output-advanced-industries-itif-report-finds/ https://www.nsf.gov/statistics/2018/nsb20181/report/sections/industry-technology-and-the-global-marketplace/highlights
claim: China represents approximately 40% of the world's technology industry.
context: Can you also acknowledge that we used to have a very large share in that market, and we no longer have a large share in that market? We can also acknowledge that China is about 40% of the world's technology industry. To concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country. It is a disservice to our national security. It is a disservice to our technology leadership, all for the benefit of one company. It makes no sense to me.

source_verification.reasoning: The ITIF source supports China's ~25% share of advanced industries. The NSF source supports China's 24% share of high-technology manufacturing. However, the note's claim about the U.S. leading in IT and information services with 36.1% is not supported by either fetched source — the ITIF page shown only contains the headline and no specific 36.1% figure for IT/information services.

citations.quote: China Now Produces Nearly One-Quarter of Global Output in Advanced Industries, New ITIF Report Finds
citations.explanation: Headline supports the note's claim that China accounts for approximately 25% of global output in advanced industries per ITIF 2026 Hamilton Index.

citations.quote: In high-technology manufacturing, the United States is the largest global producer (31% global share). The U.S. global share has remained stable for the last decade. China is the second largest global producer (24%).
citations.explanation: Supports the note's claim that China is 24% of high-technology manufacturing.
